newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline firm amid healthy demand.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline firm amid healthy demand.

text.p: NWE gasoline was firm on Friday amid healthy demand and speculation over the prospects of higher fuel taxes in Britain's post-election budget, traders said.
Eurograde barges traded twice at $202 fob AR in early trade. Later on there was talk that a barge of running refinery Eurograde material traded at $204 for first half June delivery.
A Rotterdam refiner was offering Eurograde material around $204.50 for first half June delivery, while a Norwegian player was bidding at $204.
Swaps were also stronger with some interest focused on the June/July spread after a deal was reported at $5.0.
The spread could widen further ahead of possible motor fuel tax hikes in Britain in the Labour government's post-election budget expected in June, traders said.
Traders are expecting a tax hike of two to three pence a litre which would mean gains of $35 to $50 a tonne for retailers selling material taxed at current levels after the budget.
Duty increases are usually passed directly and immediately onto the customer in Britain.
Traders were not expecting too much action in the afternoon as many players wound down positions ahead of the long weekend due to Monday's public holiday across much of Europe.
